key_insight: The paper introduces a sound way to verify AI-agent security policies when predicates or transitions are probabilistic and may be correlated, by computing worst-case upper bounds on policy-violation probability.
engineering_relevance: This gives builders of tool-using and terminal AI agents a practical runtime-monitoring method for enforcing security policies with rigorous probabilistic guarantees in messy real-world settings.
method: Formulates policy verification for probabilistic Datalog-like rules as a distributionally robust optimization problem.
Computes sound upper bounds on violation probability without relying on independence assumptions.
Targets runtime monitoring for AI agents operating over uncertain predicates such as PII detectors or declassifiers.
evidence_signal: On standard benchmarks for terminal and tool-calling agents, the method reportedly outperforms prior approaches and improves the security-utility trade-off while maintaining rigorous probability bounds.
watch_item: Soundness comes with a conservatively worst-case guarantee, so tightness of the bound and computational cost may affect deployment at scale.
paper_title: Efficient and Sound Probabilistic Verification for AI Agents
